reason: The text (Genesis 4) narrates the story of Cain and Abel, two ordinary laborers—a farmer and a shepherd—not members of an elite social class. While Cain is indeed portrayed unfavorably (he commits the first murder), this negative portrayal is not connected to any elite status. The passage makes no statement about how people of elite rank or social power are characterized; rather, it depicts the moral failure and sin of an individual. The text predates any established social hierarchies, kings, or power structures that would define 'the elite' in biblical society.
